arguments.value: Two patients from rural Ghana presented with new-onset seizures and imaging findings consistent with parenchymal neurocysticercosis. Both had epidemiologic risk factors including free-ranging pigs and pork exposure, normal laboratory studies, negative HIV testing, and no focal neurologic deficits. CT imaging showed cystic brain lesions with eccentric scolex, with one case in vesicular stage only and the other with both vesicular and calcified lesions. Both were treated with anti-seizure medication, albendazole, and corticosteroids, with no seizure recurrence on follow-up.
